title: Accounts docs
intro: Accounts is the sign-up and sign-in system of your own website and admin: one user list for your shoppers and your staff, with roles. Visitors sign in with the widget or with your own screens on the API; your server and our other products check their sign-ins offline with your website's public keys. Your website's tokens are in the Portal: open the website, then Install and tokens. The browser token is public and goes into your pages; the server token is secret and stays on your server.
localhost: Testing on your own computer: the browser token also works on pages served from localhost, *.localhost, 127.0.0.1 or [::1], on any port, over http or https. These pages use your website's real database, keys and providers, so the accounts made there are real. There is no test mode.
methods: Sign-in methods are features: Phone code (a code by SMS or WhatsApp), Email + password, Email code / magic link, Google, Apple and Facebook. Turn on the ones you want; the widget shows exactly those. Codes, magic links, password resets and invites are sent through Notifications: paste your website's Notifications server token into Connections and write these templates in Notifications (keys below, with the values each one gets). Without it, those steps answer notifications_not_connected.
social: Google, Apple and Facebook use your own app keys (Connections). Register the return address below with the provider. The widget opens the provider's page; the provider sends the person back to Accounts, which finds or creates the user and returns the browser to your page with a single-use code in the address fragment; the widget exchanges it for the sign-in.
signIns: A sign-in is a JWT signed with EdDSA (Ed25519) that lasts 15 minutes: iss is Accounts' address, aud is your website id, sub is the user id, and it carries name, email, phone and, with Roles and permissions on, role and permissions (* = every permission). The widget renews it with the user's session (session length and remember me are set per role; defaults 1 day and 30 days). Verify it on your server with the public keys (no call per check), and paste the Accounts server token into other products so they trust sign-ins too. A sign-in only says who the user is: it never authorises admin actions in any product — those need your server token or a ticket.
visitorApi: Headless: build your own screens on the visitor API with the browser token. Routes of a signed-in user also take the sign-in in the SS-Sign-In header. Sign-in routes answer { status: signed_in, signIn, expiresAt, refreshToken, sessionExpiresAt, user }, { status: two_step, challenge }, { status: two_step_setup, challenge, secret, otpauthUrl } or { status: pending }. Keep the refresh token in the browser and renew with POST /v1/session/refresh.
roles: One user list: every new sign-up gets the Customer role; GET /v1/users/count and /v1/users/counts?by=status|role count it with the list's filters (q, role, status, deletion). The ready-made roles (Owner, Business manager, Product manager, Marketing manager, Support staff) start with default permissions from Accounts, Chat, Notifications and Ecommerce (Owner has every permission), can be changed and copied, and you can add your own. A role's permissions come from the products whose server tokens you pasted into Accounts (each product publishes its list), plus your own permission names (site:<name>). A role also sets two-step (optional or required), the session length and remember me. Your admin checks the user's role and permissions before it asks a product for a ticket.
rules: Sign-up rules (Approval / invite sign-up): open sign-up, invite only, or approval required, and which standard fields are required. Custom fields (text, number, date, choice) are set in the dashboard. Security: password rules with the breached-password check, a lock after repeated wrong passwords, two-step sign-in with recovery codes, risk checks against disposable e-mail addresses and many accounts from one device or network, and terms acceptance (the version each user accepted is kept).
dataRights: Download my data gives the user one single-use link (15 minutes) to everything Accounts and every product whose token you pasted keep about them. Delete my account waits for your approval in the Users admin widget (or for the days set in Settings), then erases the user here and in every connected product; a product that cannot be reached is asked again on later requests.
activity: Activity log copy: paste this website's Accounts server token into your other products; each one then sends every staff action to Accounts: who (with the acting user's role), what, the target and its label (for example an order number), a short detail and when — never message contents, secrets or addresses. Read the copies with GET /v1/activity-copies?productId=&actor=&action=&target=&q=&from=&to= (newest first; action takes one action or several separated by commas, q searches labels, details, names and targets, from and to take an ISO-8601 time or a day in your business.json time zone) and count them with GET /v1/activity-copies/count and /v1/activity-copies/counts?by=productId|action|actor. Accounts' own log (users and roles, with each user's name or role as the label) is read with GET /v1/activity.
orders: Orders tab: paste the Ecommerce server token; My account then lists the user's last 20 orders from Ecommerce (GET /v1/customers/<userId>/orders on Ecommerce, with the server token you pasted): number, status (the status label your shop set) and total.
install: Add the script to the pages of your website and place the visitor widgets where they should appear. Widgets render nothing while their features are off or the product is stopped.
admin: Admin widgets run in your own admin with a ticket: Users (users.read to see, users.manage to block, invite, approve, change roles and notes) and Roles (roles.manage). Include the script without data-token, place the widgets and register your ticket function. The widget calls it at start and 1 minute before the ticket expires; your server checks the user's sign-in and role every time.
tickets: Your server asks for a ticket with the server token (never send the server token to a browser). The origin is the address of your admin page: any https origin, or a local one while testing. Tickets last 15 minutes and carry only the permissions of switched-on features.
business: Every product reads your business basics from https://<your domain>/.well-known/business.json. Only name is required; without the file the name is your domain and the time zone is UTC.
api: Every route answers JSON; errors are RFC 9457 problems with a stable code. Lists are paged with cursor and limit. Routes of a feature that is off answer 403 feature_off.
